Account ownership and measured gaps: Global Findex 2021 wave (Yemen fieldwork 2022–23)

01What does this evidence establish?

In the 2021 Global Findex wave for Yemen (fieldwork 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023; World Bank data year 2022), 11.9% of adults aged 15 and over in the areas the survey covered had an account at a financial institution or with a mobile-money provider. Within the same wave: 5.44% of women and 18.35% of men had an account, a difference of 12.91 percentage points; 6.5% of adults in the poorest 40% and 15.5% in the richest 60% by household income, a difference of about 9.0 percentage points; 6.98% of adults with primary education or less and 19.53% of those with secondary education or more, a difference of 12.55 percentage points; and 5.01% of adults aged 15–24 and 16.11% of those aged 25 and over, a difference of 11.10 percentage points. The survey frame excludes areas the source says represent about 23% of the population. These figures are not a 2026 rate and cannot be mapped to governorates.

Another view of the evidence
01What does this evidence establish?02What does it measure?03Who or what does it apply to?04How current is it?05What this evidence does not establish06Original source and verification07Method and verification detail

02What does it measure?

Account ownership as defined by Global Findex (the share of adults aged 15 and over in the areas the survey covered who report having an account, alone or with someone else, at a bank or another type of financial institution, or who report personally using a mobile-money service in the past 12 months), for all adults and by sex, household income, education and age (2021 Findex wave, fieldwork 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023).

03Who or what does it apply to?

Adults aged 15 and over in the areas the survey covered (the survey frame excludes areas with about 23% of the population); subgroups as defined within the same wave.

04How current is it?

These are the latest observations available for Yemen: World Bank Data reports them for 2022, from the Global Findex 2021 study fielded from 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023. The Global Findex 2025 edition adds 2024 observations for many economies but no newer observation for Yemen, so the values do not describe 2024, 2025 or 2026.

05What this evidence does not establish

These are values from one survey wave, not an annual series and not a 2026 rate. They cannot be mapped to governorates, they are not comparable with account counts reported by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden), and the differences between groups do not establish their causes.

Limits of the measure

The survey frame excludes areas holding about 23% of the population, and more than a quarter of primary sampling units were replaced. No standard errors or confidence intervals are published with these values; the Yemen sample is 1,000 respondents, so subgroup values and the gaps carry sampling uncertainty that is not quantified here.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

Weighted estimates published by the World Bank from the Global Findex survey of Yemen (1,000 respondents; fieldwork 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023; World Bank data year 2022) for all adults and for subgroups by sex, household income, education and age. Each of the four differences is calculated by this resource by subtracting the lower published value in a pair from the higher one.

When does this record change?

This record is updated when an authoritative source is revised or replaced, a newer comparable observation becomes available, the definition, population or method changes, or the conditions for public use change.

How can I verify it?

This record is drawn from the source(s) listed on this page. Open a source record to reach the original document, and check that the definition, period, population and geography match what is stated here.

How should this record be read?

Read this evidence within the definition, population or group covered, calculation base where relevant, period, geography and method shown on the page. Before reusing or comparing it, check the source, limitations, evidence date and correction history. If a value or source link is unavailable, the page says so rather than filling the gap by inference. This resource does not host source files; where an original-source link is given, check the publisher’s terms before republishing.
